title: Feds get ready to rewrite car headlight rules
gist: NHTSA is launching a negotiated rulemaking to rewrite FMVSS 108 headlight rules, aiming to harmonize with global standards and permit modern lighting such as adaptive matrix LEDs. US rules have lagged Europe partly because of the self-certification regime, and the prior ADB rule took nearly a decade.

insights.claim: NHTSA will start a negotiated rulemaking to rewrite FMVSS 108 headlight standards, saying current rules block automakers from deploying the latest safety lighting technology.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Morrison
insights.so_what: Opens the US market to advanced lighting content per vehicle.
insights.quote: Today’s standards do not allow automakers to deploy the latest safety-improving lighting technologies

insights.claim: Goals include harmonizing with global standards, updating rules for LEDs, ambient light sensors, automatic high beams and replaceable light sources, improving optics test procedures and aim, and limiting glare.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Harmonization would let OEMs ship global lighting designs to the US, lowering cost.

insights.claim: Changing FMVSS has historically been so slow that automotive lighting technology lagged in the US; adaptive beam rulemaking began after a 2013 Toyota petition and the final rule came only in 2022.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Regulatory latency has delayed US adoption of tech already common abroad.

insights.claim: Europe uses type-approval homologation while the US relies on manufacturer self-certification, which led NHTSA to reject Europe's subjective glare tests and write its own.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Structural regulatory differences explain persistent US/EU product divergence.
insights.locator: One key difference is how vehicles

insights.claim: Matrix LED headlights now on sale in the US, such as on Audi's big SUVs, are limited in functionality compared with European-spec versions.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A rewrite could unlock feature parity and software-enabled upsell.

insights.claim: The author argues skepticism of the government's streamlining push is fair, but US headlight regulations genuinely need an update.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Deregulation here is seen as substantive, not just rhetorical.
insights.locator: While it is fair to be skeptical
